subsystems.name: Atmosphere intake and separation
subsystems.role: captures and sorts the local gas into a carbon feedstock and everything else.

subsystems.name: Carbon feedstock plant
subsystems.role: breaks carbon dioxide apart so pure carbon is available to deposit.

subsystems.name: Plasma deposition head
subsystems.role: grows solid carbon layer by layer — the actual 'print head'.
parts: carbon-bearing gas feed and hydrogen line

subsystems.name: Motion and positioning
subsystems.role: moves the head, or the growing part, with micron accuracy over metres of travel.

subsystems.name: Structure and stress management
subsystems.role: keeps the printed solid from cracking as it thickens.

subsystems.name: Power and thermal
subsystems.role: plasma deposition and gas compression are power-hungry.
parts: fission surface reactor or large solar array

buildSteps.title: Characterise the local atmosphere
buildSteps.detail: Measure composition and pressure. Mars is roughly 95% carbon dioxide at about 0.6 kPa; Titan is mostly nitrogen at about 146 kPa; Venus is about 96% carbon dioxide at roughly 9 MPa. The feedstock strategy depends entirely on which of these you have.

buildSteps.title: Capture and separate the gas
buildSteps.detail: Compress the intake gas and pull out carbon dioxide with a sorbent bed or by chilling it out, leaving nitrogen, argon and traces to be vented or used separately.

buildSteps.title: Reduce carbon dioxide to carbon
buildSteps.detail: Electrolyse or chemically split the CO2 into carbon monoxide and oxygen, then reduce further to solid or gaseous carbon. On Mars the oxygen is a valuable by-product, not waste.

buildSteps.title: Grow solid carbon in a plasma
buildSteps.detail: Feed carbon-bearing gas plus hydrogen into a plasma at roughly 700–1000 °C so carbon deposits onto a seeded substrate as diamond or diamond-like carbon. Growth is slow — microns per hour in lab reactors — so a thick wall takes an extremely long time.

buildSteps.title: Address nitrogen's real role
buildSteps.detail: Nitrogen does not build a diamond lattice. In practice it is used as a dopant, as a plasma additive that changes film texture, or as a route toward hard carbon-nitride phases such as the proposed beta-C3N4 — which has never been made in bulk.

buildSteps.title: Stack layers into a shape
buildSteps.detail: Move the deposition head or the workpiece so material accumulates where the structure needs it, building walls, ribs and domes incrementally rather than as a single casting.

buildSteps.title: Control residual stress
buildSteps.detail: Diamond-like carbon films carry high internal stress and are stiff but brittle. Graded interlayers, careful temperature control and a reinforcing phase are needed to stop thick sections from delaminating or shattering.

buildSteps.title: Assemble and commission
buildSteps.detail: Join printed segments, seal and pressure-test the shell, and integrate it with power, life support and thermal systems.

prerequisites.tech: Plasma-enhanced chemical vapour deposition of diamond and diamond-like carbon
prerequisites.why: it is the only demonstrated way to grow solid carbon from a gas; today it is used for coatings and cutting tools, not structures.

prerequisites.tech: Carbon dioxide electrolysis and the reverse water-gas shift
prerequisites.why: these turn the feedstock gas into carbon and oxygen; NASA's MOXIE demonstrated CO2-to-oxygen conversion on Mars in 2021.
free-standing CVD diamond plates a few millimetres thick can be made, but structural-scale bulk material does not exist.
predicted to be superhard, but no bulk crystalline sample has been produced in decades of attempts.
fission surface-power designs have been tested on Earth, but no reactor has operated on another world.

prerequisites.tech: Robotic construction in vacuum and low gravity
prerequisites.why: demonstrated at small scale for regolith and metal printing, not for metre-scale pressure structures.

pathway.milestone: diamond and diamond-like carbon grown as micron-scale coatings in vacuum chambers
pathway.unlocks: the physics of layer-by-layer carbon deposition, at coating scale.

pathway.milestone: thicker free-standing diamond plates and scaled-up plasma reactors
pathway.unlocks: material thick enough to carry structural loads and be machined.

pathway.milestone: ISRU demonstrators that extract oxygen, water and metals from local materials on the Moon or Mars
pathway.unlocks: the gas handling, power and robotics that any printing plant needs.

pathway.milestone: a robotic testbed printing a small pressure vessel from atmospheric carbon
pathway.unlocks: evidence on whether growth rates and stress control can be pushed to building scale.
structures built where shipping them from Earth is impossible — if deposition speed, brittleness and power demands can all be solved.
